payload.title: cycle-snapshot-latest.json is never promoted: Step 4.7 names the file by WALL CLOCK, emit_pressure_state looks it up by NOMINAL TICK
payload.summary: Producer and consumer disagree on the filename key, so the promotion silently no-ops on every tick. cycle-snapshot-latest.json has been frozen since 2026-08-23T00:07:50Z (tick=00:00) — 16.5h stale as of this filing.
payload.producer: docs/agents/cowork-team/flow/tick-snapshot.md:34 — FILE_TICK=$(date -u +%H:%M), i.e. the wall clock at the moment Step 4.7 runs. Writes docs/data/cycle-snapshot-<FILE_TICK>.json.
payload.consumer: apps/mcp-server/src/.../emitPressureStateTool.ts:397 — derives HH:MM from the tick_id argument (the NOMINAL cron tick) and looks up docs/data/cycle-snapshot-<HH:MM>.json to promote it to cycle-snapshot-latest.json.
payload.why_they_diverge: Step 4.7 runs after the preflight, signal drain, cadence gates and slot claim. Any dispatch that takes longer than the drift already present pushes the wall clock past the nominal tick's HH:MM. The two only agree when Step 4.7 happens to execute inside the same clock minute as the nominal tick, which in practice never happens on a WORK tick.
live_confirmations: 2026-08-23T16:39Z (this tick) — nominal 16:30, file written as cycle-snapshot-16:39.json, emit_pressure_state returned cycle_snapshot_promoted:false. 4th observation.
3 prior observations this session, same shape, all cycle_snapshot_promoted:false
impact: The per-agent bootstrap saving this snapshot exists to deliver is never realized — every spawned agent falls through to its own get_cycle_bootstrap call (the documented Step -1 miss path). Not a blocker, but the whole feature is dark.

Worse: any consumer that DOES read cycle-snapshot-latest.json gets 16.5h-old data. telemetry.md Step 6.0's own contract reads last_regime / last_volatility_level from this file — so those two arguments have been degrading to 'unknown' on every tick rather than carrying real state forward.
payload.recommended_fix: Single-line, producer side: tick-snapshot.md's FILE_TICK should derive from the NOMINAL tick, which the dispatcher already has in hand — cowork-tick-preflight.sh's verdict JSON carries it as .tick (e.g. "2026-08-23T16:30Z"). Take its HH:MM instead of calling date -u. Fixing the consumer instead would mean guessing which wall-clock file belongs to which tick, which is strictly worse.
payload.ownership_note: Crosses two zones — the producer is a cowork flow doc (agent-father) and the consumer is TypeScript in mcp-server (dev-mcp-server). Routed to po to decompose rather than to either zone directly. The recommended fix touches only the flow doc.
payload.not_already_tracked: Checked orch-state before filing. Nearest existing rows are DESIGN-COWORK-FANOUT-T1-TICK-SNAPSHOT-WON-SLOTS (TODO, agent-father), DESIGN-COWORK-FANOUT-T2-CYCLE-BOOTSTRAP-EXTRACTION (TODO, agent-father) and SPIKE-TICK-SNAPSHOT-DEADCODE-OR-REGRESSED (CANCELLED) — none of them is this key-mismatch defect. Worth checking whether the CANCELLED spike was cancelled on the false premise that the step was dead code; it is not dead, it runs and writes every WORK tick, its output is just never consumed.
